messages:
kevin (eng-runtime): I ran an nsys capture on the dedicated pool and the perfetto timeline shows all CUDA kernels fine but CPU-side frames are almost entirely 'unknown' / no file:line. .qdrep attached. Using redwood/runtime-dev:cuda12.1 image. nsys 23.12.

kevin (eng-runtime): nsys command I used:```nsys profile --output=/tmp/run_2026 --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --cpuctxsw=false --sample=none --duration=300 --capture-range=nvtx```and then converted to perfetto with `nsys export -f traces -o run_2026.qdrep run_2026.qdrep`

perf-bot: nsys job 4821 finished :white_check_mark:

maria (eng-runtime): are those binaries built with -g? we strip symbols in the release packaging step so that would explain missing file:line on the CPU side :thinking_face:

kevin (eng-runtime): build had -g -O2 but our package step runs `strip --strip-debug libredwood_runtime.so` when making the container image. the binary inside container is the stripped artifact.

sajal (eng-ml): another common trap: CUPTI / libcupti version mismatch between host and container breaks nsys symbol correlation. run `ldd /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcupti.so` inside the container and compare to host's libcupti.

jeff (eng-infra): +1. also check the host nsys vs container toolchain. nsys needs to match host's drivers/libs for full symbol resolution. we had glibc/container libc mismatch that made perfetto show unknown frames.

maria (eng-runtime): we used to have a CI job that runs `strip` to save image size. for profiling we should publish unstripped artifacts or use split debug:```objcopy --only-keep-debug libredwood_runtime.so libredwood_runtime.debug
strip --strip-debug libredwood_runtime.so
objcopy --add-gnu-debuglink=libredwood_runtime.debug libredwood_runtime.so```

sajal (eng-ml): and for reproing hotspots, try building with `-fno-inline -fno-omit-frame-pointer` so CPU-level call stacks show clear frames (inlining hides functions so perfetto shows less useful names).

kevin (eng-runtime): noted. i also noticed the container image bundles cuda 12.1 but host driver is 12.4. could that be the issue?

jeff (eng-infra): yes. libcupti symbols are tied to driver stack. easy workaround for ad-hoc profiling: bind-mount host's libcupti into the container at runtime:```docker run --rm -v /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcupti.so:/usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcupti.so:ro -v /tmp/run_2026.qdrep:/tmp/run_2026.qdrep ...```we did this when doing perf on k8s nodes.

maria (eng-runtime): also check packaging flags: `-fno-omit-frame-pointer` is important for unwinding on x86. and don't use LTO for the profiling build (LTO can inline across modules).

sajal (eng-ml): nsys has collector knobs but i'm not sure any extra flags will fix stripped symbols. they need to be present in the binary or as separate debuglink file. for CUDA kernels you still get kernel names, but host CPU stacks (scheduler/kv cache code) need symbols.

kevin (eng-runtime): i fired `nm -C libredwood_runtime.so | grep kv_cache` and most symbols are gone in the container copy. i'll push a debug build to `ci-artifacts/profiling/` (no strip, with -g -fno-omit-frame-pointer) and re-run with the host libcupti mounted.

jeff (eng-infra): when you re-run, also capture `nsys` with `--trace=nvtx,cuda,osrt --cpuctxsw=true` to include context switches; sometimes scheduler hotspots show up there.

maria (eng-runtime): another trick: if you cannot change the binary, produce split debug and supply it to the symbolizer. perfetto/native symbolizers can consume debuginfo files if paths match or you provide symbol server.

kevin (eng-runtime): plan of action i'm taking tonight: 1) build profiling artifact (no-strip, -g, -fno-omit-frame-pointer, -fno-inline) 2) push to ci-artifacts and load into container instead of release binary 3) run docker with host libcupti bind-mounted 4) re-run `nsys profile` and export qdrep and attach here.

sajal (eng-ml): +1. also try temporarily `-fno-omit-frame-pointer -DENABLE_PROFILING` compile-time guard around heavy inlined utils that confuse the flamegraph.

kevin (eng-runtime): thanks. one weird note: perfetto shows kernel timelines from GPU perfectly aligned but the CPU flame chart shows big gaps where we expected KV cache code. I suspect batching heuristics cause GPU bursts and CPU is doing tiny fast inline ops that got optimized away. the -fno-inline run should reveal if it's a compiler-inlining issue.

jeff (eng-infra): if you still see missing lines after these steps, collect a small reproducer with debug binary and we can run `addr2line` on addresses from the .qdrep to see if resolution fails at the symbolizer step.

kevin (eng-runtime): will do, i'll upload the qdrep and the profiling binary here once done. thanks y'all, will update tonight. :pray:
